sections.trivia:
Celtic came into the game in their best position in the League for some time at third just behind Rangers. Rangers however had the hex on Celtic with 2-1, 3-0, 3-0, 3-0, 1-1 and 4-0 from their last six encounters. Celtic too were on a run not having lost since the end of September.
Celtic went with what had been their strongest side – unchanged from the last two games. Rangers had the return of Jim Baxter at left half, who had been out injured and in plaster for some time.
sections.review: This was a snatched victory for Rangers and against the run of play in the game. Celtic had plenty of chances but a lot of bad luck and Ritchie in the Rangers goal to contend with. Celtic should have put them away but failed to get the ball in the net. Jimmy Johnstone had a great game for Celtic. Fallon had scarcely one save to make other than the one that passed him from Millar – it was Millar's first goal of the season – coming from a free kick from Henderson after he was brought down by Jim Kennedy. Celtic had an out-and-out claim for a penalty in the 20th minute when Chalmers was brought down in the area by McKinnon. The only man in the ground that didn't think it was a penalty was Referee Syme, and he was the one that counted.

sections.trivia: And so to Cathkin Park the day after another unlucky defeat to the auld rival. Billy McNeill and John Clark were both out injured in the Ne'erday game. In came Jim Brogan and John Cushley. With Bobby Murdoch out injured too the forward line was rejigged with Charlie Gallacher coming in at inside left. All three players were out with ankle knocks.
sections.review:
Celtic started at full speed and pounded the Thirds goal in the first ten minutes. Then Thirds scored. They broke fast and Graham provided a needle sharp pass that took out Gemmell and there was Murray to shoot home. Celtic piled on the pressure but just like the previous day the ball would not go into the net. And just like the previous day Celtic appeared to have a perfectly good claim for a penalty turned down by the referee when Hughes went down from a McCormick tackle.
The second half started with Thirds nearly doubling their lead. The play was more even with attacks at both ends of the ground. Celtic were too often offside but in the 65th minute a Hughes shot rebounded off the post and there was Divers to put the rebound away.

sections.trivia:
John Clark, Billy McNeill and Bobby Murdoch were fit again and back in the team.
The A Reserves played Falkirk A with a team of ‘Newman’ (probably Connaghan); MacKay, O’Neill; Henderson, McNamee, J Brogan; Curley, Turner, Young, Gallacher, F Brogan. They won 4-1.
sections.review:
After an early Falkirk flurry it was all Celtic. Johnstone got the first with a classic carve-thru-the-defense run and shot. Three minutes later Jinky sent over a cross which Murdoch headed down for Chalmers to knock home. Chalmers got the third with a header from a Murdoch cross.
Hughes picked off the fourth after Gemmell fired in a cannon which Whigham parried to Johnstone and his shot came off the bar to Hughes. Four minutes later it was John Divers turn as he walked the ball around Whigham and then followed up with a second four minutes later with a carbon copy.Half time and Celtic were 6-0 up.
The situation continued in the second half with both Celtic wings in Hughes and Johnstone giving their opposite numbers serious trouble. Chalmers finally got his hatrick from a Hughes cross.

sections.trivia:
This was a Wednesday evening game with a 7:30pm kick off.
John Divers was out with 'flu. Charlie Gallacher came in for him. 
This was a repeat of the previous season's final which Third Lanark had won 2-1.
Ex-Celtic favourite Charlie Tully was appointed manager of Northern Ireland team Bangor.
Charlie Cullen who played for the Combined Reserves at inside right was suspended by the SFA Referees Committee for 7 days after being sent off in a game.
sections.review: Murdoch scored with a penalty after Chalmers was brought down in the area. Buckley scored with a left foot shot. Celtic had plenty of chances to score in the first half hour but failed to take them. Thirds got little success against the Celtic defense. McGillivray was stretchered off the field on 69 minutes and went to hospital with a head injury. Thirds played the final part of the game with 10 men.

sections.trivia:
John Fallon (ankle), Jimmy Johnstone (groin) and Bobby Murdoch (groin) all picked up knocks in the Wednesday night Galsgow Cup game against Third Lanark. John Divers was also recovering from 'flu.Fallon and Johnstone recovered in time but Paddy Turner replace Bobby Murdoch at inside right.
Outside of Celtic, Second Division Clyde were having talks to move their ground from Shawfield Stadium to a brand new stadium in East Kilbride.
sections.review: Eyemouth started well and their defense protected the goal well. With over half an hour gone and no sign of a goal the home fans began to show their unease and disenchantment. On the restart, Turner had a header off the bar then in a neat move Johnstone fired over a corner right on the head of Chalmers who easily headed home. The goal spurred Celtic on and though Eyemouth failed to buckle the Celtic attacks were now looking more menacing. Turner had a shot cleared off the line. Gallacher got a second goal with a header of 68 minutes. Chalmers got a third goal ten minutes later.

sections.trivia:
In the draw for the next round Celtic were drawn away to Morton a  Cappielow. Morton had made big progress this and last season and were  top of Division 2.
Also during the week Rangers lost their Glasgow Cup semi final against Clyde 1-0. Celtic still had to replay their drawn semi against Third Lanark.
Bobby Murdoch and John Divers were both back in training. Frank Haffey had finally had his plaster removed and given the all-clear by the hospital to start training again. With them both fit Paddy Turner and Charlie Gallacher dropped out and Celtic fielded their strongest team.
For St Mirren ex-Celt in goal Beattie had not long returned from breaking his ankle, and up front Bobby Carroll was still playing.
The ground though protected with a straw blanket was hard and showed white frost patches in places.
This was a notedly niggling match with quite a few personal battles going on and a number of 'off-the-balls' as well as disputes between the referee and players. Clark opf St Mirren was sent off and Hughes was booked.
sections.review:
Chalmers missed an early open goal as did Hughes who replaced him in the centre. On ten minutes Divers gave a diamond pass to Chalmers and Stevie fired home. St Mirren's response barely got off the ground. St Mirren had Clark sent off for wreckless behaviour when he piled into Hughes who was on the ground and a "rugby style scrum" ensued". St Mirren played the remainder of the first half and the whole of the second with 10 men. 
In the second half it was a return to the familiar ground of Celtic having lots of chances but failing to convert any. The game was generally very niggley with both sides having chips at each other. Fifteen minutes from time Jinky hit a lob from Divers home on the volley. And just before the whistle Divers himself scored.

sections.trivia:
This was a replay of the semi final played at Celtic Park on the 8th January which ended in a 1-1 draw.
Jimmy Johnstone was rested for the game with Charlie Gallacher coming in at outside right.
sections.review: A noticeably better performance from Celtic that the one in the first game at Celtic Park. Murdoch got the opener from a header from a Gallacher corner. With the lead established Celtic gained the upper hand and from that point onwards Thirds were on the back foot. It took till eleven minutes into the second half though to score a second. This came when John Hughes took a long pass from McNeill, made his space and scored. All round the team looked good with McNeill and Young standing out in defense. Again this was another niggley game with a number of personal feuds going on around the ground. Celtic were lucky not to concede a penalty when Gemmell brought down Anderson down in thye first half and this was the flag for the fouling and hacking to begin. Referee Brittle was lenient and failed to get on top of the infringements which therefore multiplied. By the end Hughes and Murdoch came off with injuries that were a worry for Saturday's Cup game against Morton.

sections.trivia:
This was an all-ticket game with a maximum crowd set at 22,000. Also the game was to kick off at 2:30pm so that the game would start and finish in daylight. The game was a sell-out.
Despite a physically hard game on Monday night in the replayed Glasgow Cup semi final against Third Lanark, everyone came thru OK and a full strength team was expected.On the Friday before the game John Divers reported with a damaged ankle which apparently was picked up in the Third Lanark game and he failed to pass a fitness test. Charlie Gallacher stood in for him.
Morton were the dominant team in the second Division, top of that league and pushing for promotion as well as losing finalisats in this season's League Cup. They played a full strength side with the son of an ex-Celt at right back.
Away from Celtic, ex-Celt Bertie Auld was suspended by the English FA for a month after getting sent off for Birmingham City in their match against Fulham. Johnny Haynes and Bertie had been involved in an altercation. Haynes struck Auld after provocation then Bertie stuck the heid on Haynes and then struck Cook of Fulham. Haynes was suspended for a week. Another ex-Celt Pat Crerand was also suspended for 7 days following a separate sending off in the Manchester Utd – Burnley Boxing Day game.
Frank Haffey was back in action playing for the A Reserves away to Arbroath A Reserves in a team of Haffey; Halpin, Parkes; Cattenach, Cushley, O'Neill; Curley, Turner, McCallum, Gnaulati, Brady.
sections.review:
Billed as a thriller from the start this game lived up to it's expectations. Three players were booked – Chalmers and Hughes of Celtic and Wilson of Morton. Murdoch missed a penalty shortly before half time. Celtic were under the cosh for a great proportion of the first half. McGraw, who was carried off with a leg injury just before the end, got the first goal for Morton on 22 minutes. Celtic settled and equalised through Hughes with a brilliant goal beating three defenders, to make the half-time score even. 
In the second half Charlie Gallacher scored direct from a corner and Jinky added the insurance three minutes later. McGraw had the ball in the back of the Celtic net but was offside. Hughes had a great game for Celtic.

sections.trivia:
The draw for the next round of the Scottish Cup was made and Celtic were drawn at home against Airdrie. Airdrie had had a bye in the first round and beaten Alloa in the second.
John Divers was fit again recovered from the ankle knock. John Hughes reported for treatment after the Morton game but was back training on Tuesday. The team stayed the same with Gallacher in at inside left.
Bobby Murdoch, John Hughes and Jimmy Johnstone were selected for the Scotland U23 side to face England U23 at Newcastle
There was a 1 minute silence before kick off as a tribute to Eddie Dowie, a former Dunfermiline player who had recently died.
sections.review: Dunfermiline started well and attacked Fallon's goal. In the 11th minute McNeill headed a ball back under pressure from Dickson. The ball bounced off of Fallon then off of Mcneill's knee and into the net.(Some reports give Dickson the goal). Jinky was giving Lunn a run around on the right wing. In the second half Celtic went all out in attack confident that McNeill could marshall the Dunfermiline attack and Celtic defense. Despite all the attacks and shots Celtic could not find a way though.

The A Reserves played Aberdeen A with Haffey; J. Halpin, O'Neill; Henderson, McNamee, J Brogan; Lennox, Young, Tommy Spencer, Turner, David Brady. They won 3-1. 
The Combined Reserves faced Raith Rovers with Madden; 'Newman' (possibly Jim Craig), Parkes; Cattanach, Cushley, McCarron; John McGuire, Curley, Charles Cullen, Gerrard Gillan, Stephen Gnaulati. They won 4-0.
There was no news about the team in the week. However a fit again Divers came in with Gallacher dropped out and Frank Brogan was in at outside left with Hughes missing with 'flu.
sections.review:
The first part of the game was back and forth with both teams having shots. Celtic gained the upper hand when Smith attempting to clear a ball shot the ball into his net. The rest of the half proved to be an evenly matched affair.
In the second half Brogan scored a good goal from a Divers pass, and Divers himself scored before the end with a 20 yard shot.

sections.trivia:
Neil Mochan rejoined Celtic as an Assistant Trainer to Sean Fallon.
John Hughes had recovered from 'flu and was back training. On the Wednesday before Ian Young was ordered to bed to hopefully recover in time for the game. He recovered in time for the game and with Hughes back on the left hand side, Celtic were back to their full strength team. Airdrie also fielded a full strength team which included 4 from the team that had been thrashed 9-0 in the league back in October – Keenan, ex-Celt Jimmy Rowan, Hannah and Murray.
Billy Price handed in a third transfer request which was finally agreed to and he was released on a free. He was then handed a £5 fine by the SFA for being sent off in a Reserve game. Third Lanark and Morton were said to be interested in his services.
Ex-Celt Mike Jackson was transferred from St Johnstone to Third Lanark in an exchange for Ken Brownlee plus £1500.
sections.review:
Celtic started the better and pounded the Airdrie goal and on 10 minutes they were ahead when Chalmers received a ball in his stride and shot home a 20 yarder. Gradually Airdrie got back into the game and there were a few scares in the Celtic goal. Hughes was injured close to the end of the half and went off for treatment but was soon back in time to see Airdrie claim for a penalty against Gemmell which was waved away by the referee.
Shortly after the restart Hughes was flattened in the area and Murdoch put the spot kick away. It was all Celtic now but Airdrie pulled one back when Jimmy Rowan won out in a goal mouth tussle. Despite it appearing more even Celtic scored twice more through Johnstone and then late in the game with Hughes, despite Clark going off with an injury ten minutes from the end.
The man behind most of this win was John Divers, sitting as he did for much of the season slightly deeper he was able to direct pplay and become the link man. He didn't score but a lot of the moves started through him.

sections.trivia:
Celtic counted the cost of the Cup win against Airdrie with Murdoch having injured his shoulder, Hughes injured (bruised ribs) and John Clark (leg knock) having to go off with an injury at the end of the game. All three failed fitness tests before the game. For Murdoch, back in came Paddy Turner; for Hughes, Frank Brogan and a debut at right half for Sam Henderson. Dundee Utd had an even harder task with on the injury list from their usual first team.
The draw was made the Quarter finals of the Scottish Cup and in the hot ball-cold ball scenario Celtic were drawn against Rangers away at Ibrox.
The SFA proposed a new tournament to be run in May with 6 teams playing out along the lines of the League Cup.
Billy Price was given the offer of moving to Third Lanark and was considering it.
The game was played on a bitterly cold night.
sections.review: A poor game all in all with not much to cheer about other than two points in the bag. Turner and Brogan started brightly but faded. Sam Henderson showed promise but also inexperience and left gaps at the back. Celtic's goal came from Chalmers header of a Jimmy Johnstone cross. Dundee Utd with a depleted team defended well. They had at least three chances to equalise andf failed to take them. Jimmy Johnstone was the most exciting player on the park.

sections.trivia:
Tommy Gemmell injured his leg in the Wednesday night game against Dundee Utd. Gemmell pulled through and took his place in the game. Jimmy Johnstone was rested and in his place came Charlie Gallacher.
Snow started to fall on the night before the game throughout Scotland. Most games went ahead with a few delays. This game was delayed by 16 minutes whilst the groundsmen worked fuiriously to clear the lines. Snow fell throughout the game.
sections.review:
All the players of both sides found the conditions tricky and slippery underfoot in the snow. In such conditions the game became a bit of a lottery. Airdrie's new centre forward Marshall proved to be a handful to the Celtic defenders. At the other end Chalmers and Divers had chances. In the 20th minute a shot from Brogan produced a goal mouth melee – Chalmers is credited with the goal in some reports but most give it to Brogan. 
For the second half the snow abated meaning the game could be played to the end. Divers started a move which saw Brogan take on the defense before cutting in and shooting a curling dipping shot which Samson could do little about.. 2-0. Shortly after he very nearly did exactly the same but this time Samson got morte on the ball and managed to push it wide. As the game progressed Celtic became more and more dominant. Just before the whistle Brogan won a penalty when he was hauled down by the goalkeeper. He took the kick himself and it was saved.

sections.trivia:
The draw had been made back in December. The other ties were Manchester Utd v Sporting Lisbon, Hamburg or Barcelona v Olympic Lyon, MTK Budapest v Fenerbahce. On paper Celtic were pretty evenly matched with Slovan.
The Slovan stars were centre half Popluhar, and goalkeeper Schroiff, both of whom were Czech internationals. They were generally a physically big team. They arrived on the Monday night by charter flight to Renfrew Airport.
Slovan players stayed up late the night before the agme to watch Cassius Clay beat Sonny Liston in Miami for the world heavyweight boxing title.
They were given a bus tour of West of Scotland ‘beauty spots’ before the match.
Future Celtic manager Jozef Venglos was dropped for this game in favour of Horvath.
Legendary Celt Chic Geatons watched from the stand.
Celtic played their strongest side having rested Jimmy Johnstone from the Saturday snow-affected game against Airdrie and Clark, Murdoch and Hughes were back fit again.
The full Scotland side face the Scottish League at Ibrox on the Monday night with no Celtic players picked in view of this tie on the Wednesday night.
Outside of the immediate, Dunfermiline announced that Jock Stein would quit as their manager at the end of the season.
sections.review:
Slovan returned to Czechoslovakia from Renfrew airport confident of overturning Celtic’s slender lead from this game.

The Czechs defended resolutely led by their class captain Popluhar and and Celtic were left to rue missed chances. Divers and Murdoch failed to make an impact and Hughes faded particularly in the second half. This left Chalmers starved up front for support.

Hughes struck the bar in the opening minute and in the second half Murdoch had an incredible miss with an open goal.

In 70 minutes Filo fouled Chalmers in the area and Murdoch smashed home the resultant penalty for Celtic to win on the night.

sections.trivia:
Bobby Murdoch (bruised foot), Billy McNeill (back) and John Hughes (still problems with injured ribs) all came out of the midweek ECWC game against Slovan Bratislava with inuries and were on the treatment table. Murdoch and Hughes both passed fitness tests but McNeill was out with John McNamee returning. 
East Stirling had the worst defensive record in the league.
The A Reserves played East Stirling's A Reserves with a team of Haffey; MacKay, O'Neill; J Brogan, Cushley, Price; Lennox, Cattanach, Spencer, Turner, F Brogan. Celtic won 3-2.
sections.review:
The first two goals came from a Murdoch – Chalmers double act with Murdoch supplying the ball and Stevie Chalmers finishing. Fallon had an easy first half in goal. Murdoch got the third goal after a move between Hughes and Chalmers. Right before half time East Stirling pulled one back through Coburn.
Celtic took up where they left off with East Stirling trying to play the offside trap. Chalmers got his hatrick with a pass from Hughes. Hughes was pulled down by the goalkeeper when he was clear through on goal and Bobby Murdocvh converted the spot kick. Kemop pulled one back before the end.
At the end of the month Celtic were third in the table having won 4 and lost 1 league games.

sections.trivia:
Celtic flew to Vienna and travelled the final 40 miles to Bratislava by bus.McNeill travelled though he was now in plaster for his back injury. He had a fitness test before the game and was ready.
  The summer cup is initiated but Celtic will not play in it if they qualify again for Europe.   
  Game kicked off at 1.30 GMT. as the stadium had no floodlighting.
After the game Stevie Chalmers 'claimed' the match ball. The officials went as far as going into the Celtic changing room to try and retrieve the ball but aftyer a bit of bargaining Chalmers was allowed tyo keep it.
In the banquet after the game for both teams each Celtic player was presented with a set of cut glass wine goblets and the club with a magnificent cut glass vase.
sections.review:
This was a night of glory for Celtic as Slovan were hot favourites to win.  
The pitch in the Pehelne Pole stadium was in good condition after worries about frost.
Celtic stood firm in the first half with Clark, McNeill and Kennedy forming a fine defensive barrier in front of Fallon.
In the second half Slovan upped the tempo and Fallon was forced into making a couple of good saves.
With time running out and the home fans becoming irritable Hughes beat Moravcik on the half way line and ran half the field before scoring to the delight of the Celtic players. It was a sensational goal and Celtic were through.

Evening Times 5th March 1964

sections.trivia:
The team returned from Bratislava on Wednesday evening and were driven to Celtic Park where the floodlights were turned on and the team met the supporters. No one had realistically supposed that Celtic would beat Slovan and that they were through to the semi final of a European competition came as something of a surprise to many. The reality was that in their second season in European football Celtic had managed to get through to a semi final of a European competition.
The Slovan game had produced a few injuries. John Clark picked up a leg injury. John Divers picked up an 8 inch gash down one leg. Ian Young damaged his shoulder. Divers and Young recovered but Clark was out and a reshuffle saw Murdoch move to right half with Frank Brogan coming in at outside right and Jimmy Johnstone moving in one.
Rangers players lined up before the match and clapped the Celtic players on to the pitch in view of Celts reaching the ECWC semi finals against MTK Budapest. This was regarded as a fine gesture of sportsmanship.
sections.review:
Celtic put Rangers under early pressure after the embarassment of being heralded onto the field. Rangers soaked up the pressure and attacked on the break. Henderson for Rangers and Johnstone for Celtic both had the right ideas and troubled their opposite numbers. The goal came when a corner from the left was flighted over and Fallon palmed it out for Forrest to head home. On the restart Henderson added a second, an excellent goal where he picked the ball up 40 yds from goal and advanced with the Celtic defense retreating and unleashed an unstoppable shot from the edge of the box. Celtic rejigged with Johnstone going back to outside right, Hughes going to centre forward and Brogsan over to the left wing, but they were no more successful with this line-up than the original. Murdoch then picked up a booking. Chalmers was aslo booked towards the end.
In the light of this defeat – the sixth straight defeat in a row by Rangers – there were calls for Celtic to invest in a forward. The defense it was felt was sound and a unit but an fully experienced and finished forward was needed.

Ex-Celtic player Bobby Craig who had been swapped to St Johnstone at the start of this season, was moved on by St Johnstone to Oldham Athletic
sections.review:
The game started slowly and poorly with both sides showing little connection between front and back and the passing being woeful. But the game changed in character on the half hour mark when Jimmy Johnstoner hit the post with the Jags defense well beaten. From the resulting corner Divers scored with a 25 yard shot. Celtic then took the upper hand for the rest of the half without scoring.
In the second half Duffy scored a well-worked goal for Thistle with a cross from Cowan being headed back across goal by Hainey from Duffy to head into the top corner. Cowan then doubled the score and it was Partick's turn to dominate. Celtic however managed to equalisde when Hughes won a ball and crossed for Murdoch to shoot home from 20 yards.

The game was played in the rain
In the Reserve game played at Easter Rd Celtic fielded Haffey; Parkes, O'Neill; Cattanach, McNamee, J Brogan; F Brogan, Turner, Tommy Spencer, Gallacher, Lennox. They won 5-3.
sections.review:
Celtic won a penalty after three minutes when Baxter handled a Kennedy cross. Celtic continued at a fast pace and Simpson had to save from Johnstone and Chalmers. In the fifteenth minute Celtic won a free kick when MacKay was fouled with the referee booking MacKay for something he said after the incident. Johnstone and Baxter were also at each other and both received lectures from the referee. At half time there was still just the one goal in it.
Chalmers got a second from a Murdoch pass. However Hibs were not giving up and had a good share of possession but no real threat in front of goal. Divers added a third and Chalmers and Murdoch added two late goals to give Celtic a very satisftying 5-0 win
Hibernian at this time were managerless and their veteran 'keeper Ronnie Simpson was performing miracles in goal. Their main problem was not a lack of footballing skill but a toothless attack.

sections.trivia:
Seen as a League decider by many in Scotland with Rangers playing Dunfermiline and Rangers and Kilmarnock first and second respectively with four p[oints between them.
Both A Reserves and Combined Reserves were in action; the A Reserves played Kilmarnock with Connaghan, Parkes, O'Neill, Cattanach, McNamee, J Brogan; Curley, Turner, Tommy Spencer, Gallacher, F Brogan. They won 4-1. The Combined Reserves played Queen's Park with Madden, J. Halpin, McCarron, Jim Orr, Cushley, Allan Lawson, John McGuire, John McCallum, Charlie Cullen, Gerrard Gillan, Stephen Gnaulati. They also won 4-1.
John Clark had recovered from his knee knock and came back in at right half in place of Duncan MacKay. Both teams were pushing and it still looked an even game.
Off the field, the second of the Clyde Tunnels was opened and traffic started to use the tunnels in both directions. Calls were still heard though for a new bridge across the Clyde.
sections.review:
Celtic were bright early on but as the first half wore on Kilmarnock established a surety on the ballwith McInally always dangerous. He set up the opener for Murray on sixteen minutes. Celtic should have replied when Hughes broke free but he elected to shoot over with teammates in better positions. Both teams fought hard for the rest of the half with Celtic having good chances and though Kilmarnock went in a goal up it looked an even tussle with Celtic pushing hard for an equaliser.
A degree of tetchiness had started to creep into the game with King booked for Killie and Kennedy and McFadzean having a personal duel. But on 64 minutes Killie found the killer when Mcfadzean crossed and Murray hit the ball strongly past Fallon. Two minutes later Murray set up McInally with a hint of offside. from a fighting 1 goal down Celtic were now three behind. The fight went out and McInally added a fourth with 18 minutes to go.
Celtic were a well beaten team after starting well and holding their own for much of the game.

sections.review:
A fairly dull and unsatisfying match throughout the first half. Clyde, as the second division side, played onfident football without being able to penetrate the Celtic defense. Celtic in contrast were back to their profligacy in front of goal whenever they had the chance and McCulloch in the Clyde goal dealt with everything that came his way.
In the second half the pattern continued to the growing disenchantment of a good crowd. But on 55 minutes Chalmers rose to head home a Hughes corner home and five minutes later Divers picked on a loose ball in the Clyde area after a Murdoch shot from a Chalmers quick throw in and slotted the ball home.

On fifteen minutes they had doubled their advantage when Chalmers headed a free kick from Kennedy back across for Jinky to tap home. and three minutes later Chalmers added a third from a Clark pass. The announcement was made that Jock Stein, former Celtic player and future manager, would become the manager of Hibernian. Stein anounced that he would effectively leave Dunfermiline at the end of the season. Dunfermiline were hardly happy that the decision to miove to Hibs was announced and allowed him to leave early and take control at Easter Rd. He was on a reported salary of £70 per week.
An announcement was made by the new Celtic Development Fund that the Jungle would be redeveloped and a new stand would be built. Other plans included better approaches, better parking and improved covered areas. The person running the scheme was former Celtic goalkeeper John Bonnar. Members payed a shilling each week and a draw was made every week with the first prize being £100, the second £80 and the third £40 with consolation prizes and awards to the seller of the winning ticket.
Celtic delayed announcing the team till before kick off. In the end it was an unchanged team that played.
Celtic's 2-1 win here took them into second place in the league above Kilmarnock though having played one game more.
sections.review:
Celtic began well in their usual bustling style but were met by a well ordered Dundee defense. In the 18th minute Gilzean broke with the ball and laid it out to Penman, and then was in the perfect place to head his cross past Fallon. Dundee continued to have the better of the play throughout the remainder of the first half and well into the second. But they could not beat Fallon again and Celtic were just as troubled in front of the Dundee goal. Chalmers was roundly booed for five minutes with the number of easy chances he missed.
Fifteen minutes from time Gallacher scored a thrilling goal with a 35 yard shot which shook life into both teams and it was Chalmers who got the winner for Celtic just before the end.

sections.trivia:
Celtic had an 11 day gap between this game and their previous against St Johnstone away in the League on 4th April. That time was used for training and practise matches on the field at Celtic Park. However Billy McNeill and Jim Kennedy played for Scotland in a 1-0 win over England at Hampden on 11th .
This was Celtic’s first appearance in a European semi final.
MTK were a club as old as Celtic and were founded in 1888. They had also won 9 Hungarian league championships in a row between 1917 and 1925. MTK had reached the semi final with wins over Slavia Sofia, Motor Zwickau and needed a replay to overcome Fenerbahce
Celtic had a full scale training session at Parkhead at 3pm in an effort to find peak form that night.
Celtic’s pre match meal was fillet steak, toast and tea.
MTK arrived in Glasgow late on the Monday afternoon. They were given two hours in Glasgow for souvenier hunting on the afternoon before the game.
MTK were without three of their stars – outside right Sandor, wing half Kovacs, and Laczke – all were out injured. This still left three internationals in their team – Keszel, Vasas and Nagy.
For Celtic Gemmell was back fit at left back; and though Divers was missing, Gallacher stepped in and John Hughes came back in at outside left.
sections.review:
Contemporary reports stated that Celtic relied on ‘determination, relentless aggression and pace’ rather than skill against the Hungarians.

After a dull first half Celtic led 1-0 after Johnstone scrambled the ball home after keeper Kovalic fumbled a Clark shot.

In the second half Johnstone and Chalmers went up a gear and Johnstone was the subject of tough tackling from the MTK defenders.In 65 minutes Chalmers scored with a low shot and eleven minutes leader he headed a Murdoch cross in off the far post.

Murdoch, Gallagher and Chalmers all missed further chances and Celtic were indebted to Fallon who made two fine saves near the end.

Celtic were now clear favourites to win through to the final in Brussels in May.

sections.review: Celtic thoroughly outplayed Hearts in the first half on the base of an early goal from Stevie Chalmers coming from a Jimmy Johnstone cross. Despite plenty of pressure in the first half they could not find a second. When they took their foot off the gas in the second half with Hearts clearly upping their game the inevitable equaliser came from Hamilton, who had switched wings with Traynor. Thereafter though they tried to push the pace they just could not get back ahead.

sections.review:
This was one of the worst nights Celtic have ever experienced in their history. The defeat was a catastrophe and the management were criticised for their naive tactics of playing an open game with a 3-0 lead behind them.   
Only 10,000 fans turned out and the game was played on a firm, dry pitch which suited MTK's style. The Hungarian capitaL had been bathing in a heat wave through much of the week.
In 11 minutes Kuti scored and with the experienced winger Sandor looking influential Celtic were under constant pressure.
They rallied later in the half with Johnstone almost creating a chance for Hughes and they then had two goals disallowed to offside through Johnstone and Hughes.
In the second half Celtic continued to attack and Chalmers had a strong shot saved.
In 47 minutes Vasas scored from the penalty spot after Gemmell had punched a shot over the bar on the goal line.
As Celtic faltered MTK went for broke and scored twice more through Sandor and Kuti.
This was a devastating blow as Celtic were expected to reach the final in Brussels against Sporting Lisbon on May 13 1964.

In later years Billy McNeill recalled the disastrous events of Budapest: 
'If ever an inexperienced side got to a European semi-final it was the Celtic team of that season.
We took a 3-0 lead in the first leg with one goal by Jimmy Johnstone and two by Stevie Chalmers but then went to Budapest with no idea of what European football was all about and how to defend it.
We played it like a pre-season friendly, lost a goal in 11 minutes and before we knew we were out the tournament by 61 minutes.
There was a suspicion by Celtic officials that the ref had been got at by the home side, but it was no one's fault but our own.
MTK were a competent side but not brilliant and it was a poor and inexperienced display by us. It was only our second season in Europe, and it showed.'
